newsitem.title: UK: Tyson's infamous bite was double strength - magazine.
newsitem.headline: Tyson's infamous bite was double strength - magazine.

text.p: The bite with which Mike Tyson took off a chunk of fellow heavyweight Evander Holyfield's ear was probably delivered with twice normal force, New Scientist magazine said on Thursday.
Tyson was disqualified for biting Holyfield's ears in their title fight in Las Vegas on Saturday, earning him widespread condemnation in the world of boxing and beyond.
Most people generate forces equivalent to around 10 kilos when they bite with their incisors, Tom Korioth of the University of Minnesota's Dental School said.
But having watched the video of Tyson munching Holyfield's ear, he estimated that the forces involved must have been twice as strong.
"He was shearing and tearing, which is almost alligator-like," Korioth was quoted as saying by the magazine.
"Most of the ear is cartilage and you need a lot of power to bite through it."
Holyfield, who required reconstructive surgery to mend his ear, said on Tuesday he held no grudges against Iron Mike after the incident.
